content: Welcome to Senda. It's good to be here with you on the very first step of this path. Today, we begin a new journey, not by adding anything, but by simply discovering what's already here.

Our only goal today is to gently rest our attention on the breath. Meditation isn't about stopping your thoughts or feeling a certain way; it's just the practice of paying attention, on purpose. Your mind will wander, and that is a normal and expected part of the process. Let's begin.

First, find a comfortable position, either sitting upright in a chair with your feet flat on the floor, or on a cushion. Allow your hands to rest easily in your lap and your back to be straight but not stiff.
And when you're ready, gently close your eyes, or if you prefer, just lower your gaze and rest it softly on the floor in front of you.
Take one slightly deeper breath in through the nose... and as you breathe out, just let go of any obvious tension you might be holding.
Now, let your breath settle into its own natural, easy rhythm. No need to control it at all.
Bring your awareness to the physical feeling of the breath in your body.
You might notice it as the gentle rise and fall of your stomach.
Or maybe you feel the slight expansion of your chest.
Just choose whichever sensation is most clear to you, and gently rest your attention there.
Simply noticing the feeling of one breath in...
...and the feeling of one breath out.
Inevitably, you'll notice your mind has wandered away from the breath. This is not a mistake. It is the practice.
The moment you realize you're thinking is a moment of awareness.
With kindness, just acknowledge where your mind went, and then gently guide your focus back to the sensation of your next breath.
Now, gently release your focus on the breath.
For a few moments, just sit. Noticing the feeling of the air on your skin, the sounds around you, the state of your mind. Just being aware.
When you feel ready, you can slowly and gently open your eyes, bringing your awareness back to the room.
You have just completed the first practice. The goal was not perfection, but simply to begin. To show up, pay attention, and gently come back. You have done that.
As this practice ends, the journey continues. Thank you for walking this first step of the path with me today.
